mcp.guide:
## How to work with Workboard
- Workboard is the app where the user tracks each work item: a folder with the status in the frontmatter of its README.md and the tasks under `## {tasks}`.
- Status, type, environments, notes (one-line summary), branch and tasks are read and changed ONLY through the `workboard` MCP tools: {session}, {get}, {update}, {addTask}, {completeTask}, {addNote} and {markRan}. Do not edit the README frontmatter by hand.
- When you start, call {session}: it returns the work items of this session, their folders and their tasks.
- States: {states}. Types: {types}. Environments: {environments}.
- Agreed date (YYYY-MM-DD) and agreed hours also go through {update}, but only if the user gives them: do not estimate them yourself.
- If you find something left to do, add it as a task. When you finish a step, update the status and the summary.
- You can only write the work items of this session.

### Files of each work item
- Scripts and documents of a work item go in ITS folder. In a group session (`grp-…` folder), what belongs to one item goes in that item's subfolder and what is shared goes in the group folder.
- Workboard groups files by a word in their name: MIGRATION_ / SEED_ / ROLLBACK_ (migrations), FIX_ (fixes), DIAG_ / VERIF_ (diagnostics), PLAN_ / HANDOFF_ / QA_ and .md (documentation); code (.py, .ps1…) goes to scripts. Use those prefixes unless the project defines its own convention.
- Workboard records which scripts ran in which environment. The user marks it: if they tell you they ran a script, record it with {markRan}. Never mark it on your own.
- Do not move, rename or delete work folders: grouping and deleting are done from Workboard.

### Tools
- The user promotes useful scripts from earlier sessions as tools. Before writing a script for something repetitive, check {listTools} and, if there is one, run it with {runTool}.

agent.gap.plan: the ## {heading} section of the README is empty
agent.gap.tasks: there are no open tasks under ## {tasks}
agent.planIncomplete: Workboard: the plan is not complete yet ({gaps}). Complete it in the item's README (## {heading}) and load the tasks with {addTask} before finishing.
agent.planMissing: Workboard: when the previous turn ended, the plan was missing this: {gaps}.
agent.otherItem.one: [Workboard] The request mentions {list}, which is not part of this session. Don't edit it from here (the MCP won't let you write it). If it has to be worked on, tell the user to add it with «Add to session» or to open a session for that item; if it is only mentioned as a reference, carry on.
agent.otherItem.many: [Workboard] The request mentions {list}, which are not part of this session. Don't edit them from here (the MCP won't let you write them). If they have to be worked on, tell the user to add them with «Add to session» or to open a session for them; if they are only mentioned as a reference, carry on.
agent.itemsAdded: [Workboard] {count} item(s) were added to this session. You can now read and write them with the `workboard` MCP:
agent.itemRemoved: [Workboard] The user removed item {item} from this session. Don't keep working on it from here: you can no longer write to it.
agent.itemSplit: [Workboard] Item {item} was split into another session («{name}»). Don't keep working on it from here: you can no longer write to it.
agent.itemsMoved: [Workboard] The user moved folders of this session's items. Use the new paths:
agent.handoff: [Workboard] This session is long and will continue in a new one. Before stopping, update the summary of each item with {update} and load what is left as tasks ({addTask}), with the detail needed to pick it up without this conversation. Don't start another task.
agent.continue: You are continuing the work of the session «{name}», which was cut because it was long. Call {session} and pick up from the status, summary, plan and tasks of your items. If something is unclear, ask me before redoing work.

session.notInSession: {item} is not part of the session

session.nothingToSplit: The session has a single item: there is nothing to split
session.noConversation: The session has no conversation to inherit yet: create a new session for that item
session.notRunning: The session is not running: resume it first
session.busy: Wait until the session finishes what it is doing
session.noProcess: The session has no running process
session.rec.saved: The README was updated after the last code change: what matters is already saved.
session.rec.stateChanged: An item changed status in this session and {why}: ask for a handoff and continue in a new one.

session.rec.inProgress: You are in the middle of something and {why}: compact to keep going without losing the thread.
session.rec.why.code: there is code the README doesn't reflect yet
session.rec.why.chat: what was done is only in the conversation

git.notInstalled: git is not installed or not on the PATH
git.notReadOnly: git {cmd} is not a read-only command
promo.flag.shared: also on branch {branch} (stacked on another feature?)
promo.flag.sameMessage: {target} already has a commit with the same author and message
promo.flag.mergeFromEnv: merge from {env} into the branch: brings {env} code that may not be in {target}
promo.flag.mergeOther: merge of another branch: its commits don't come alone; -m 1 brings its whole change
promo.warn.noBase: Could not find where the branch starts (missing fetch of the environments, or too old): no commits are proposed from it.
promo.warn.unpushed: The local branch has unpushed commits: they are included (they are in your repo) but not on the remote.
promo.warn.envMerges: The branch has {n} merge(s) from another environment: if later commits use that code and it is not in {target}, the cherry-pick may not build.
promo.warn.sameContent: The files the branch touched are already the same in {target} (squash or manual merge?): its commits are left unchecked.
promo.note.alreadyCp: {n} commit(s) are already in {target} through an earlier cherry-pick -x.
promo.note.fastForward: The branch has no commits of its own outside the main line (fast-forward merge, or empty).
promo.note.nothing: Nothing to promote: the work is already in {target}.
promo.note.mentionsDone: The {source} commits that mention the item are already in {target}.
git.noOwnCommits: No branch of {item} has commits of its own in the configured repositories
git.tip.merged: The branch's own commits are in {env}
git.tip.equivalent: Each own commit has an equivalent in {env} (cherry-pick)
git.tip.content: The files the branch touched are identical in {env} (squash or manual merge)
git.tip.mentioned: A commit in {env} mentions the item in its message
git.tip.pendingUnknown: Not in {env} (the branch's own commits could not be isolated)
git.readOnly: Read-only: it never fetches; fetch in the repositories for fresh data.
git.noIds: This folder has no item id. The panel looks for branches whose name contains the id.
git.loading: Reading the repositories… The first time can take a while; then it uses a cache.
git.desync: {env}: {ok} already has the work, {missing} does not. They are merged together.
git.fetchHint: The app never fetches: the data is as fresh as your last fetch
git.ownHint: Commits of the branch itself (not what it brought from the main line)
git.noBranches: No branches with the item id.
git.nothingFound: No branch or commit in the repositories mentions {ids}.
git.noRepos: No repositories: add them in Settings (Git repositories).
git.settingsDetected: Repositories next to the work folder of {root}, detected by their environment branches. Edit them and save to set them by hand.
git.settingsCustom: Repositories set by hand for {root} and the remote branch of each environment.
git.envRefsHint: Remote branches that identify each environment, comma-separated: the first one that exists wins.
git.alreadyAdded: That repository is already on the list
promo.noIds: None of the chosen folders has an item id
promo.noTargets: The workflow needs at least two environments to promote
promo.buttonHint: Cherry-pick or merge commands to promote
promo.modeHint: Cherry-pick: only the item's missing commits. Merge: the item's whole branch (brings everything on it).
promo.staleFetch: Last fetch of {repo}: {ago}. Run git fetch --all and recompute.
promo.oneRepo: #{id} only has a branch in {repo}: make sure it has no changes in another repository.
promo.nothing: Nothing to promote: everything of {ids} is already in {env}.
promo.notIncluded: Not included ({n}) · doubtful, check them if they go
promo.cmd.conflict: If a cherry-pick conflicts: resolve it, git add and git cherry-pick --continue; then run the push.
promo.footer: The app runs nothing: you copy the commands and run them. It uses cherry-pick -x.
alerts.gitDesync: Repositories out of step in an environment
alerts.gitDirty: Uncommitted changes on the item's branch
